subject: accounting
description: Accounting skill tree, FET (CAPS Accounting Grades 10-12). Tiers = CAPS terms (T1-T4) within each grade. 51 atomic skills across the three grades, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order (each skill lists the previous CAPS-order skill as a prerequisite; the first skill of each grade has none). Mastery = 60% of a 20-item pool (FET rule, no timer). Tap-based mechanics only (no free-text / typed numbers): choice, true-false, cloze, sequence, image-match, sort-buckets, highlight-source, argument-builder, paragraph-template, source-comparison, plus two Accounting-specific mechanics — equation-effect (effect of a transaction on Assets / Owner's equity / Liabilities) and double-entry (which account is debited and credited). Questions live in data/accounting-question-bank.json.

levels.title: Grade 10 — Accounting
levels.description: Foundations of Financial Accounting for a sole trader, plus the three managing-resources and managerial topics. T1: indigenous vs formal bookkeeping, ethics, GAAP, internal control, accounting concepts, the full bookkeeping cycle (source documents, cash & credit journals, ledgers, Trial Balance) and the accounting equation. T2: VAT, salaries & wages, year-end adjustments and final accounts. T3: financial statements and their analysis. T4: cost accounting and budgeting concepts. 19 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Concepts, GAAP, control & bookkeeping of a sole trader

atomic_skills.title: Informal vs formal bookkeeping
atomic_skills.description: Comparison of the bookkeeping of the informal/indigenous sector and the formal sector: the concepts capital, fixed assets, stock, cost price, labour cost, selling price, income, expenses and profit; how resources are managed; and the process of determining selling prices, cost of sales, labour costs, income and expenses.

error_signatures.description: Confuses cost price with selling price when working out profit
error_signatures.example: Says profit is the selling price, ignoring the cost price

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Profit = selling price − cost price. The informal trader still tracks the same things a formal business does, just without formal books.

atomic_skills.title: Code of ethics in the financial environment
atomic_skills.description: The code of ethics applicable to all parties in the financial environment and the basic principles of ethics: leadership, discipline, transparency, accountability, fairness, sustainability and responsible management. Ethics is integrated across all topics.

error_signatures.description: Cannot match an ethical principle to a workplace example
error_signatures.example: Calls hiding information from owners 'transparency'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tie each principle to a plain test: transparency = nothing hidden; accountability = answerable for your actions; fairness = same rules for all.

atomic_skills.title: GAAP principles
atomic_skills.description: Definition and application of the Generally Accepted Accounting Practice principles: historical cost, prudence, materiality, business entity rule, going concern and matching. Applied to all relevant topics.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the business entity rule with the going-concern principle
error_signatures.example: Says business entity means the business will continue operating indefinitely

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Business entity = the owner and the business are separate. Going concern = the business will keep operating. Matching = record income with the expenses that earned it.

atomic_skills.title: Internal control basics
atomic_skills.description: What internal control means and the basic internal control processes: control environment, risk assessment, control activities supported by policy and procedures, information and communication, and monitoring of performance. Integrated with other topics.

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify which control process an example belongs to
error_signatures.example: Calls a stock count 'risk assessment' rather than a control activity

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Division of duties, authorisation, and physical controls are control ACTIVITIES. Spotting what could go wrong is risk ASSESSMENT.

atomic_skills.title: Accounting concepts & the accounting cycle
atomic_skills.description: Definition of accounting concepts up to financial statements — debit, credit, equity, capital, assets, liabilities, ledger, journal, profit, loss, VAT, income, expenses, final accounts, financial statements, discounts, the accounting cycle, financial vs managerial accounting and the perpetual inventory system.

error_signatures.description: Misclassifies an item as an asset/liability/income/expense
error_signatures.example: Calls a loan from the bank an asset

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Assets are what the business owns/controls; liabilities are what it owes; income increases equity; expenses decrease it.

atomic_skills.title: Source documents & double entry
atomic_skills.description: The source documents that start each transaction and the double-entry principle — every transaction has an equal debit and credit. Links each document to the journal it feeds.

error_signatures.description: Records both entries on the same side
error_signatures.example: Debits both bank and sales for a cash sale

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Every transaction has TWO sides — one debit and one credit of equal value. If both are on the same side, it cannot balance.

atomic_skills.title: Cash journals (CRJ, CPJ, Petty Cash)
atomic_skills.description: Recording cash transactions in the Cash Receipts Journal, Cash Payments Journal (including loans, fixed deposits, interest income and expense, dishonoured cheques, discount allowed and received) and Petty Cash Journal.

error_signatures.description: Records a receipt in the payments journal or vice versa
error_signatures.example: Puts rent paid in the Cash Receipts Journal

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Money IN → Cash Receipts Journal. Money OUT → Cash Payments Journal. Small cash payments → Petty Cash Journal.

atomic_skills.title: Credit journals (DJ, DAJ, CJ, CAJ, GJ)
atomic_skills.description: Recording credit transactions in the Debtors' Journal, Debtors' Allowances Journal, Creditors' Journal and Creditors' Allowances Journal, and the General Journal entries for bad debts, interest on overdue accounts, cancellations of discount on dishonoured cheques and corrections of errors.

error_signatures.description: Confuses selling on credit with buying on credit
error_signatures.example: Records goods sold on credit in the Creditors' Journal

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sold goods on credit → Debtors' Journal. Bought goods on credit → Creditors' Journal. Returns reverse into the matching Allowances journal.

atomic_skills.title: Posting to ledgers, Trial Balance & control lists
atomic_skills.description: Posting journals to the General, Debtors' and Creditors' Ledgers, drawing up a Trial Balance, and preparing debtors' and creditors' lists to reconcile with the control accounts (including correcting errors and omissions).

error_signatures.description: Trial Balance does not balance because a posting went to the wrong side
error_signatures.example: Posts a debit ledger total into the credit column of the Trial Balance

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Trial Balance debit total must equal the credit total. The debtors'/creditors' list total must equal its control account balance.

atomic_skills.title: The accounting equation
atomic_skills.description: Analysing transactions of a sole trader and showing their effect on the accounting equation (Assets = Owner's equity + Liabilities) for all transactions up to financial statements.

error_signatures.description: Changes only one side of the equation
error_signatures.example: Increases assets for a cash sale but leaves owner's equity unchanged

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Every transaction keeps A = OE + L in balance. If assets go up, something else must change by the same amount.

tiers.title: Term 2 — VAT, salaries & wages, adjustments & final accounts

atomic_skills.title: VAT basics
atomic_skills.description: The basic concepts of Value-Added Tax: the need for, purpose of and principles of VAT, zero-rated items, VAT-exempt items, standard-rated (VAT-able) items and the current VAT rate.

error_signatures.description: Confuses zero-rated with exempt supplies
error_signatures.example: Says financial services are zero-rated rather than exempt

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Zero-rated = taxed at 0% (e.g. brown bread, maize meal). Exempt = outside VAT (e.g. some financial services). Standard-rated = the current VAT rate.

atomic_skills.title: Salaries & wages
atomic_skills.description: Calculating and recording salary and wage scales and payments: normal time, overtime, deductions (PAYE, pension fund, UIF, medical aid, union membership) and employer contributions (pension, UIF, medical aid, skills development levy), posted through the journals to the ledger.

error_signatures.description: Treats an employer contribution as an employee deduction
error_signatures.example: Subtracts the skills development levy from the employee's gross pay

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Deductions come OUT of the employee's gross pay. Contributions are an EXTRA cost paid BY the employer on top of gross pay.

atomic_skills.title: Year-end adjustments (sole trader)
atomic_skills.description: Year-end adjustments: trading stock deficit/surplus, consumable stores on hand, depreciation (cost/straight-line and diminishing balance), bad debts and bad debts recovered, correction of errors, accrued income, income received in advance, prepaid and accrued expenses, and interest on a mortgage bond.

error_signatures.description: Treats accrued expenses as prepaid (or vice versa)
error_signatures.example: Treats rent still owing at year-end as a prepaid expense

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Accrued = owing/earned but not yet paid/received. Prepaid/received-in-advance = paid/received but not yet used/earned. Match each to the correct period.

atomic_skills.title: Final accounts & Trial Balances
atomic_skills.description: The pre-adjustment Trial Balance, closing transfers, the Trading Account and Profit and Loss Account, the post-adjustment and post-closing Trial Balances, and the reversal of certain adjustments at the start of the next period.

error_signatures.description: Closes off a balance-sheet account into the Trading Account
error_signatures.example: Transfers the equipment balance to the Trading Account

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Only nominal (income/expense) accounts close off to Trading or Profit and Loss. Balance-sheet accounts carry their balance forward.

atomic_skills.title: Income Statement (sole trader)
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the Income Statement (Statement of Comprehensive Income) of a sole trader from the adjusted figures, with the supporting notes.

error_signatures.description: Places a balance-sheet item in the Income Statement
error_signatures.example: Lists the bank loan as an expense in the Income Statement

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Income Statement shows only income and expenses for the year. Assets, liabilities and equity belong on the Balance Sheet.

atomic_skills.title: Balance Sheet & notes (sole trader)
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the Balance Sheet (Statement of Financial Position) of a sole trader and its notes from the adjusted figures.

error_signatures.description: Balance Sheet does not balance
error_signatures.example: Total assets do not equal owner's equity plus liabilities

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Assets = Owner's equity + Liabilities, always. Use the notes (fixed assets, trade & other receivables, etc.) to build each total.

atomic_skills.title: Analysis & interpretation of financial statements
atomic_skills.description: Calculating and interpreting financial indicators: gross profit on sales, gross profit on cost of sales, net profit on sales, operating expenses on sales, operating profit on sales, current ratio, acid-test ratio, solvency ratio and return on equity.

error_signatures.description: Reads a worsening ratio as an improvement
error_signatures.example: Says a current ratio falling from 2:1 to 0.8:1 shows better liquidity

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Liquidity ratios (current, acid-test) should comfortably cover what is owed; profitability percentages should hold or rise. Compare to last year and to a benchmark.

atomic_skills.title: Cost accounting concepts (manufacturing)
atomic_skills.description: Basic cost concepts of a manufacturing business: direct and indirect labour, direct (raw) and indirect materials, factory overhead costs, prime cost, variable costs, fixed costs and work-in-process.

error_signatures.description: Classifies an indirect cost as a direct cost
error_signatures.example: Calls the factory cleaner's wage direct labour

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Direct costs can be traced straight to the product (raw materials, machine operators). Indirect costs (factory rent, cleaning) support production but are not in the product itself.

atomic_skills.title: Budgeting concepts
atomic_skills.description: Basic budgeting concepts: the cash budget, zero-based budget, capital budget, long-term budget and medium-term budget.

error_signatures.description: Confuses a cash budget with a projected income statement
error_signatures.example: Includes depreciation as a payment in the cash budget

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A cash budget only tracks money actually flowing in and out. Non-cash items like depreciation never appear in it.

levels.title: Grade 11 — Accounting
levels.description: Partnerships, clubs, manufacturing and the managing-resources topics. T1: ethics, internal audit, bank & creditors reconciliations, fixed assets, and the full partnership cycle to financial statements. T2: partnership analysis and clubs (non-profit organisations). T3: cost accounting, budgeting and inventory systems. T4: VAT calculations. 16 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Ethics, audit, reconciliations, fixed assets & partnerships

atomic_skills.title: Ethics in the financial environment
atomic_skills.description: Identifying and analysing ethical behaviour in financial environments with reference to accountability, transparency and sustainability, integrated through appropriate scenarios.

error_signatures.description: Cannot justify why an action is unethical
error_signatures.example: Calls a conflict of interest acceptable because it is profitable

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Judge against accountability, transparency and sustainability. If an action hides information, harms stakeholders, or is not sustainable, it is unethical.

atomic_skills.title: Internal audit & control
atomic_skills.description: Internal audit processes: the meaning of an internal audit, the difference between internal control and an internal audit, the role of the internal auditor, division of duties, documentation and physical controls, and audit procedures for cash, credit, stock, debtors and creditors.

error_signatures.description: Confuses internal control with internal audit
error_signatures.example: Says the internal auditor performs the daily authorisation of payments

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Internal CONTROL is the day-to-day system that prevents errors/fraud. Internal AUDIT independently checks that the controls are working.

atomic_skills.title: Bank reconciliation
atomic_skills.description: Reconciling the bank statement with the cash journals to prepare a bank reconciliation statement: outstanding deposits, cheques not yet presented, stop/debit orders, direct transfers, bank charges, interest, errors and omissions, R/D or cancelled cheques and post-dated cheques.

error_signatures.description: Adds an item that should be subtracted on the reconciliation
error_signatures.example: Adds outstanding cheques to the bank statement balance

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Outstanding deposits are added and unpresented cheques subtracted from the bank statement balance. Bank charges and interest update the cash book.

atomic_skills.title: Creditors reconciliation
atomic_skills.description: Reconciling statements received from creditors with the accounts in the Creditors' Ledger to prepare creditors' reconciliation statements: outstanding invoices or credit notes, outstanding payments, discounts not recorded, and the correction of errors or omissions.

error_signatures.description: Adjusts the wrong record for a discount not yet recorded
error_signatures.example: Changes the creditor's statement instead of the ledger account

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Find the difference, decide which record is wrong, and correct that one. The reconciled creditor's account must agree with the supplier's statement.

atomic_skills.title: Fixed/tangible assets
atomic_skills.description: The fixed/tangible asset register, recording the acquisition of assets, calculating and recording depreciation (straight-line and diminishing balance), how fully depreciated assets are shown, and recording the disposal of assets (cash, credit, trade-in) at the start, during and end of a financial year.

error_signatures.description: Forgets to record depreciation up to the date of disposal
error_signatures.example: Disposes of a vehicle without first writing off the current year's depreciation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: When disposing of an asset, first record depreciation up to the disposal date, then transfer cost and accumulated depreciation to the Asset Disposal account.

atomic_skills.title: Partnerships: concepts & GAAP
atomic_skills.description: Concepts unique to partnerships — partnership, capital accounts, current accounts, interest on capital, salaries and bonus to partners, division of profits/losses — together with the GAAP principles applied to partnerships.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the capital account with the current account
error_signatures.example: Records a partner's salary in the capital account

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Capital accounts hold the fixed contributions. Current accounts hold the year's profit share, salaries, interest on capital and drawings.

atomic_skills.title: Partnerships: ledger, adjustments & final accounts
atomic_skills.description: The partnership accounting cycle, year-end adjustments (including provision for bad debts, salaries and bonus to partners, interest on capital and interest on loan), and the Trading, Profit and Loss and Appropriation accounts.

error_signatures.description: Stops at net profit and omits the appropriation of profit
error_signatures.example: Does not divide the profit between the partners

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: After the Profit and Loss Account gives net profit, the Appropriation Account shares it: partner salaries, interest on capital, then the remaining profit in the agreed ratio.

atomic_skills.title: Partnerships: financial statements & notes
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the Income Statement and Balance Sheet of a partnership and the supporting notes (including the partners' current accounts), and reversing certain adjustments at the start of the next period.

error_signatures.description: Omits the current accounts note from the Balance Sheet
error_signatures.example: Shows owner's equity without the current account movements

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Partnership equity = capital accounts + current accounts. The current accounts note shows salaries, interest, profit share and drawings for each partner.

atomic_skills.title: Partnerships: analysis & interpretation
atomic_skills.description: Analysing and interpreting partnership financial statements: the Grade 10 indicators plus stock turnover rate, stock holding period, average debtors' collection period, average creditors' payment period, debt-equity ratio (gearing), partners' earnings and return on partners' equity.

error_signatures.description: Interprets a high gearing ratio as automatically good
error_signatures.example: Says more debt always means a healthier business

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Gearing measures reliance on borrowed funds; high gearing is risky if returns fall. Compare each indicator to last year and to the cost of borrowing.

atomic_skills.title: Clubs (NPO): concepts
atomic_skills.description: Concepts unique to non-profit organisations (clubs): non-profit organisation, constitution, accumulated fund, membership fees, entrance fees, affiliation fees, honorarium, surplus and deficit.

error_signatures.description: Treats the accumulated fund as profit
error_signatures.example: Calls the accumulated fund the club's profit for the year

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A club has no profit. Its capital is the accumulated fund, and its result for the year is a surplus or deficit, not a profit or loss.

atomic_skills.title: Clubs: cash book, ledger & Statement of Receipts and Payments
atomic_skills.description: The accounting cycle for clubs: the analysis cash book, posting to the ledger (accumulated fund, membership fees, entrance fees and trading accounts such as refreshments), the Trial Balance, the Statement of Receipts and Payments, and the difference between receipts & income and payments & expenses.

error_signatures.description: Confuses receipts with income
error_signatures.example: Treats a loan received as income in the club's results

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Receipts and payments are cash movements; income and expenses belong to the period. A loan received is a receipt but not income.

atomic_skills.title: Cost accounting: calculations
atomic_skills.description: Calculating, in a manufacturing environment, variable and fixed costs, the cost of a product using variable and fixed costs, unit cost, contribution per unit and the break-even point.

error_signatures.description: Uses total fixed cost instead of contribution per unit in the break-even formula
error_signatures.example: Divides fixed costs by selling price rather than by contribution per unit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Contribution per unit = selling price − variable cost per unit. Break-even units = total fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit.

atomic_skills.title: Manufacturing ledger accounts
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the ledger accounts of a manufacturing business: the Balance Sheet section (raw material, work-in-progress, finished goods and consumable stores stock), the nominal accounts section (sales, cost of sales, raw materials issued, factory wages, factory electricity and rent, depreciation) and the cost accounts section (direct materials, direct labour, factory overhead, administration and selling & distribution cost).

error_signatures.description: Allocates a factory cost to administration
error_signatures.example: Puts factory rent under administration cost

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Factory-floor costs are factory overheads; office costs are administration; getting goods to customers is selling & distribution.

atomic_skills.title: Budgeting: cash budget & projected income statement
atomic_skills.description: Preparing and presenting a cash budget for sole traders (projected receipts and payments, projected debtors' collection and creditors' payments) and a Projected Income Statement (projected revenue and expenditure).

error_signatures.description: Includes a credit sale as a receipt in the month of sale
error_signatures.example: Records the full value of credit sales as cash received immediately

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The cash budget records cash when it is actually received or paid. Credit sales become receipts only when debtors pay, per the collection pattern.

atomic_skills.title: Inventory systems: perpetual vs periodic
atomic_skills.description: Defining the perpetual and periodic stock systems, their advantages and disadvantages, and recording transactions under the periodic system compared with the perpetual system: purchases account vs Trading Stock account, opening and closing stock accounts, the Trading Account, carriage on purchases and customs & import duties.

error_signatures.description: Uses a Trading Stock account under the periodic system
error_signatures.example: Records purchases into Trading Stock when the periodic system is in use

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Perpetual = stock updated with every transaction (Trading Stock account). Periodic = a Purchases account is used and stock is counted at period-end.

atomic_skills.title: VAT calculations
atomic_skills.description: Performing VAT calculations using the current rate: adding VAT to cost price plus mark-up, extracting VAT from a VAT-inclusive amount, working on an invoice or receipt basis, and the effect of bad debts, discounts and goods returned on VAT, with the related ethics and internal control.

error_signatures.description: Takes 15% of the inclusive amount instead of extracting VAT
error_signatures.example: Multiplies a VAT-inclusive total by 15% to find the VAT

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: To ADD VAT: amount × 15%. To EXTRACT VAT from an inclusive amount: amount × 15/115.

levels.title: Grade 12 — Accounting
levels.description: Companies, close corporations and the full managing-resources and managerial set, building to the NSC examination. T1: company bookkeeping, financial statements (including the Cash Flow Statement), interpretation and published statements. T2: professional ethics, fixed assets, close corporations, controls, inventory valuation, reconciliations and the VAT control account. T3: cost accounting and budgeting analysis. Term 4 is examination revision (no new content). 16 atomic skills, progression-gated in CAPS teaching order.

atomic_skills.title: Companies: concepts & unique accounts
atomic_skills.description: Concepts unique to companies: public and private companies, the Companies Act, the Registrar of Companies, the Memorandum of Incorporation, income tax and provisional tax, dividends, shares, issue price, earnings, shareholders, directors, auditors, limited liability, the separation of ownership from control, retained income, authorised and issued share capital and the JSE.

error_signatures.description: Confuses authorised with issued share capital
error_signatures.example: Says issued capital is the maximum the company may ever sell

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Authorised = the maximum number of shares the company MAY issue. Issued = the shares actually sold to shareholders.

atomic_skills.title: Companies: bookkeeping
atomic_skills.description: The accounting cycle for a company, including issuing shares at issue price (no par value or share premium under the Companies Act), buying back shares, loans and interest (mortgage interest capitalised), income tax, dividends, directors' fees and audit fees.

error_signatures.description: Treats dividends as an expense in the Income Statement
error_signatures.example: Lists dividends among the operating expenses

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Dividends are a distribution of profit, not an expense. They are appropriated after profit, not deducted in the Income Statement.

atomic_skills.title: Companies: adjustments & final accounts
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the final accounts of a company with year-end adjustments (including those for income tax and the declaration and payment of dividends), and the Trading, Profit and Loss and Appropriation accounts, with reversals.

error_signatures.description: Omits the income tax adjustment before appropriation
error_signatures.example: Appropriates profit without first accounting for company tax

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Company profit is taxed: account for income tax to reach profit after tax, then appropriate dividends and retained income.

atomic_skills.title: Companies: financial statements & Cash Flow Statement
atomic_skills.description: Preparing the detailed financial statements of a company — the Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement — together with the notes.

error_signatures.description: Places a financing cash flow under operating activities
error_signatures.example: Shows proceeds from a new loan as an operating cash flow

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Cash Flow Statement has three parts: operating (trading), investing (assets) and financing (shares and loans). Place each flow in the right section.

atomic_skills.title: Companies: analysis & interpretation
atomic_skills.description: Analysing and interpreting the Income Statement, Balance Sheet and notes, including the earlier indicators plus debt-equity ratio (gearing), return on shareholders' equity, return on total capital employed, net asset value per share, dividends per share and earnings per share.

error_signatures.description: Confuses earnings per share with dividends per share
error_signatures.example: Says EPS is the cash each shareholder receives

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: EPS = total earnings ÷ shares (profit attributable per share). DPS = dividends actually declared ÷ shares (cash returned per share).

atomic_skills.title: Analysis of published statements & audit reports
atomic_skills.description: Analysing a company's published financial statements and annual report: the Directors' Report, the Independent Auditors' Report, the abridged Income Statement, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Statement, and information on governance and the company's activities.

error_signatures.description: Misreads the meaning of an unqualified audit report
error_signatures.example: Says an unqualified report guarantees the company is profitable

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An unqualified (clean) audit report means the statements fairly present the position — not that the company is doing well. Read the Directors' Report for performance.

tiers.title: Term 2 — Ethics, fixed assets, close corporations, control, inventory, reconciliations & VAT

atomic_skills.title: Professional ethics & company legislation
atomic_skills.description: The role of professional bodies (SAICA, SAIPA), disciplinary and punitive measures for non-compliance with the Code of Professional Conduct, the King Code III, and the basic principles of the Companies Act (directors' performance evaluation, remuneration policies, dispute resolution, business rescue, conflict of interest and responsibilities of directors).

error_signatures.description: Cannot link a governance failure to a King III principle
error_signatures.example: Says directors have no accountability to shareholders

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: King III rests on responsibility, accountability, fairness and transparency. Directors must act in the company's best interest and answer for it.

atomic_skills.title: Fixed assets: interpretation
atomic_skills.description: Interpreting and reporting on the movement of fixed assets: the age of assets, the replacement rate and the life span of assets, with GAAP, ethics and internal control integrated.

error_signatures.description: Reads a low replacement rate as healthy without context
error_signatures.example: Says not replacing any assets is always good for cash flow

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Compare the rate of replacement to the rate of wear and age. Failing to replace ageing assets risks breakdowns and lost production.

atomic_skills.title: Close corporations
atomic_skills.description: Concepts unique to close corporations — close corporation, founding statement, members, loans to and from members, and distribution to members — and the differences between the financial statements of companies and close corporations, particularly in terminology.

error_signatures.description: Uses company terminology for a CC
error_signatures.example: Refers to 'shareholders' and 'share capital' in a close corporation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A CC has MEMBERS and members' contributions, not shareholders and share capital. Distributions go to members, not dividends to shareholders.

atomic_skills.title: Internal control & audit (companies)
atomic_skills.description: Applying internal control and internal audit processes in a business: the means of gathering audit evidence, the basis for audit samples, basic sampling techniques, internal audit reports and the accountable management of resources, plus the difference between internal and external auditors.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the role of the internal auditor with the external auditor
error_signatures.example: Says the external auditor runs the company's daily controls

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Internal auditors work FOR the company checking controls all year. External auditors are independent and give an opinion on the annual statements.

atomic_skills.title: Inventory valuation
atomic_skills.description: Validating, valuing and calculating inventories using the perpetual and periodic systems: specific identification of cost price per unit, first-in-first-out (FIFO) and the weighted-average method, with GAAP, ethics and control integrated.

error_signatures.description: Applies LIFO assumptions when FIFO is required
error_signatures.example: Values closing stock using the oldest prices under FIFO

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FIFO: the first units bought are sold first, so closing stock is valued at the MOST RECENT prices. Weighted average uses one blended cost per unit.

atomic_skills.title: Reconciliations: analysis & interpretation
atomic_skills.description: Analysing and interpreting bank, debtors' and creditors' reconciliations: reconciling creditors' statements with their accounts, reconciling debtors' and creditors' lists with the control accounts, and analysing and interpreting a debtors' age analysis and bank reconciliation statements.

error_signatures.description: Cannot draw a conclusion from a debtors' age analysis
error_signatures.example: Ignores that most debt sits in the 90+ day column

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: An age analysis shows how overdue debtors are. Debt sitting in the 60/90+ day columns signals poor collection and a higher risk of bad debts.

atomic_skills.title: VAT control account
atomic_skills.description: Calculating the amount payable to or receivable from SARS and completing the VAT control ledger account from given information, with ethics and internal control over the collection and payment of VAT.

error_signatures.description: Treats input VAT as an amount owed to SARS
error_signatures.example: Adds VAT on purchases to the amount payable to SARS

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Output VAT (on sales) is owed TO SARS; input VAT (on purchases) is claimed BACK. Amount payable = output VAT − input VAT.

atomic_skills.title: Production Cost Statement
atomic_skills.description: Preparing a Production Cost Statement with notes for the manufacturing costs of a business, and calculating the total cost of production.

error_signatures.description: Omits work-in-progress adjustments from the cost of production
error_signatures.example: Ignores opening and closing work-in-progress

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cost of production of finished goods = direct materials + direct labour + factory overheads, adjusted for opening and closing work-in-progress.

atomic_skills.title: Unit costs, break-even & cost control
atomic_skills.description: Preparing a short-form Income Statement with notes for administration and selling & distribution cost, calculating gross profit on finished goods sold, variable and fixed costs, cost per unit, contribution per unit and the break-even point, and interpreting the results.

error_signatures.description: Cannot interpret production against the break-even point
error_signatures.example: Says producing below break-even still yields a profit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Above break-even = profit; below = loss. Compare units produced/sold to the break-even units to judge whether the business covers its costs.

atomic_skills.title: Budgeting: analysis & interpretation
atomic_skills.description: Analysing, interpreting and comparing Projected Income Statements and cash budgets for sole traders or companies (receipts, payments, debtors' collection, creditors' payment and cash balances), and comparing budgeted to actual figures as a control.

error_signatures.description: Treats a favourable variance as automatically good
error_signatures.example: Praises spending far below budget on repairs without questioning why

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Compare budget to actual and ask WHY. Underspending on maintenance or wages may signal neglect, not good control.
